    "def choose(obs):",
    "    drugs = obs['drugs']",
    "    preds = obs['predictions']",
    "    qf = set(obs['queried_f'])",
    "    qm = set(obs['queried_m'])",
    "    avail_m = set(obs['available_m'])",
    "    budget = obs['budget_left']",
    "    costs = obs['costs']",
    "    # functional candidates not yet functionally queried",
    "    f_cands = [d for d in drugs if d not in qf]",
    "    # affordable functional queries",
    "    f_aff = [d for d in f_cands if costs['f'] <= budget]",
    "    if not f_aff and budget < costs['f'] and budget < costs['m']:",
    "        return {'kind': 'stop'}",
    "    # If no functional candidate is affordable, we may still buy molecular info",
    "    # only if it can plausibly change which functional drug we pick later.",
    "    # Estimate uncertainty: spread of predictions among f_cands.",
    "    def spread(cands):",
    "        if not cands:",
    "            return 0.0",
    "        vals = [preds[d] for d in cands]",
    "        return max(vals) - min(vals)",
    "    def top_gap(cands):",
    "        if len(cands) < 2:",
    "            return 1.0",
    "        vals = sorted((preds[d] for d in cands), reverse=True)",
    "        return vals[0] - vals[1]",
    "    # Decide whether a molecular query is worth it.",
    "    # Molecular queries are useful when:",
    "    #  - we have budget to spare beyond the functional queries we can still do,",
    "    #  - the top functional predictions are close (low confidence / high ambiguity),",
    "    #  - the molecular drug is a plausible competitor (high prediction or similar to top).",
    "    # We only spend on 'm' if it leaves enough budget for at least one 'f' afterwards",
    "    # OR if no 'f' is affordable at all and 'm' is the only way to learn.",
    "    m_cands = [d for d in avail_m if d not in qm and costs['m'] <= budget]",
    "    # Score functional candidates: prediction, with tie-break on prior and nn to favor",
    "    # likely positives (objective = distinct confirmed positives).",
    "    prior = obs.get('prior', {}) if isinstance(obs.get('prior'), dict) else {}",
    "    nn = obs.get('nn', {}) if isinstance(obs.get('nn'), dict) else {}",
    "    def f_score(d):",
    "        p = preds.get(d, 0.0)",
    "        pr = prior.get(d, 0.0) if isinstance(prior, dict) else 0.0",
    "        n = nn.get(d, 0.0) if isinstance(nn, dict) else 0.0",
    "        # emphasize prediction but blend in priors to break ties toward likely positives",
    "        return p + 0.05 * pr + 0.05 * n",
    "    # If we have affordable functional candidates, consider whether a molecular query",
    "    # would improve selection enough to justify the cost.",
    "    # Conditions for molecular query:",
    "    #   (a) there is at least one affordable m candidate,",
    "    #   (b) after spending on m, we can still afford at least one f (or m is only option),",
    "    #   (c) ambiguity among top f candidates is high (top gap small) OR",
    "    #       the m candidate is itself a strong f candidate whose functional label would",
    "    #       be informative (we'd still query it functionally later).",
    "    if m_cands:",
    "        # best f candidate score",
    "        best_f = max(f_aff, key=f_score) if f_aff else None",
    "        gap = top_gap(f_aff) if f_aff else 1.0",
    "        # Candidate m drugs that are also f candidates (dual-value)",
    "        dual = [d for d in m_cands if d in f_aff]",
    "        # Can we still do a functional query after paying for m?",
    "        can_f_after = (budget - costs['m']) >= costs['f']",
    "        # If no f affordable at all, m is the only learning channel.",
    "        if not f_aff:",
    "            # Only spend on m if it might reveal something; pick highest-pred m drug.",
    "            m_drug = max(m_cands, key=lambda d: preds.get(d, 0.0))",
    "            return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': m_drug}",
    "        # With f affordable:",
    "        # Spend on m if ambiguity is high (small gap) and we can still f afterwards,",
    "        # and prefer dual-value m drugs (which are also strong f candidates).",
    "        if can_f_after and gap < 0.15 and len(f_aff) >= 2:",
    "            # pick the m drug that is most likely to be a positive functional hit",
    "            # (highest f_score among m_cands), preferring dual-value drugs.",
    "            def m_score(d):",
    "                base = f_score(d)",
    "                bonus = 0.1 if d in f_aff else 0.0",
    "                return base + bonus",
    "            m_drug = max(m_cands, key=m_score)",
    "            return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': m_drug}",
    "        # Also spend on m if a dual-value drug is available and its f_score is close to best,",
    "        # i.e., molecular info could resolve which of two near-equal candidates to trust.",
    "        if can_f_after and dual:",
    "            # check if any dual drug is within 0.1 of best_f score",
    "            if best_f is not None:",
    "                bf = f_score(best_f)",
    "                close_dual = [d for d in dual if bf - f_score(d) < 0.1]",
    "                if close_dual and gap < 0.2:",
    "                    m_drug = max(close_dual, key=m_score)",
    "                    return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': m_drug}",

    "def choose(obs):",
    "    budget = obs['budget_left']",
    "    preds = obs['predictions']",

    "    qf = set(obs['queried_f'])",
    "    qm = set(obs['queried_m'])",
    "    avail_m = set(obs.get('available_m', []))",
    "    costs = obs['costs']",
    "    cf = costs.get('f', 1.0)",
    "    cm = costs.get('m', 0.5)",
    "    if budget < min(cf, cm):",
    "        return {'kind': 'stop'}",
    "    cand_f = [d for d in drugs if d not in qf]",
    "    cand_m = [d for d in drugs if d not in qm and d in avail_m]",
    "    def score_f(d):",
    "        p = preds.get(d, 0.0)",
    "        return p",
    "    def score_m(d):",
    "        p = preds.get(d, 0.0)",
    "        return p",
    "    best_f = None",
    "    if cand_f and budget >= cf:",
    "        best_f = max(cand_f, key=lambda d: (score_f(d), -cf))",
    "    best_m = None",
    "    if cand_m and budget >= cm:",
    "        best_m = max(cand_m, key=lambda d: (score_m(d), -cm))",
    "    if best_f is None and best_m is None:",
    "        return {'kind': 'stop'}",
    "    if best_f is None:",
    "        return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': best_m}",
    "    if best_m is None:",
    "        return {'kind': 'f', 'drug': best_f}",
    "    pf = score_f(best_f)",
    "    pm = score_m(best_m)",
    "    step = obs.get('step', 0)",
    "    prior = obs.get('prior', {})",
    "    nn = obs.get('nn', {})",
    "    base_f = prior.get(best_f, pf)",
    "    base_m = prior.get(best_m, pm)",
    "    lift_f = pf - base_f",
    "    lift_m = pm - base_m",
    "    n_f = len(qf)",
    "    n_m = len(qm)",
    "    hit_rate_hint = 0.0",
    "    if n_f > 0:",
    "        hit_rate_hint = 0.5",
    "    explore_bias = 0.0",
    "    if n_f == 0:",
    "        explore_bias = 0.15",
    "    elif n_f < 2:",
    "        explore_bias = 0.05",
    "    f_value = pf + lift_f * 0.5 + explore_bias",
    "    m_value = pm * 0.9 + lift_m * 0.3",
    "    if n_m == 0 and n_f > 0:",
    "        m_value += 0.05",
    "    if budget < cf + cm:",
    "        if pf >= pm - 0.05:",
    "            return {'kind': 'f', 'drug': best_f} if budget >= cf else {'kind': 'm', 'drug': best_m}",
    "        else:",
    "            return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': best_m} if budget >= cm else {'kind': 'f', 'drug': best_f}",
    "    if f_value >= m_value:",
    "        return {'kind': 'f', 'drug': best_f}",
    "    return {'kind': 'm', 'drug': best_m}"
  ],
  "rationale": "This policy compares the best affordable functional candidate and the best affordable molecular candidate using current predictions, prior baseline, and a small exploration bonus for functional queries early on. Molecular queries are only used when their predicted probability is competitive and they haven't been queried yet, and budget constraints force a choice when only one action remains affordable. This balances the confirmed-hit objective with occasional low-cost molecular updates."
}
